text:
that's true and thanks for that
but the problem here was....


When you measured the output with the DMM
IT WAS NOT CLEAR ON YOUR DMM IF YOU WERE MEASURING V AC or V DC


all we could see was a cheap , no name multimeter that was showing 15.3  V
but we couldn't actually see the setting


now.. yes
common sense dictates that a bridge rectifier with a smoothing capacitor will produce DC Output
but... THIS IS A TUTORIAL and you didn't show that very clearly


your wave shape video was a lot better , in my opinion
i mean for the kiddies that don't know how it works, it's always better to have a scope to show it




and in my opinion it's much better to first show
Half Wave Rectification (so they understand how the negative half of the wave is removed)
and then to see a pulsating DC without the inverted rectified waves
and to also show them the power loss through a diode.


then ......you bring in the bridge rectifier so that the purpose is made clear
- that we get the inverted portion of the wave on the positive cycle
- that we don't lose half our power in rectification
- and that the capacitor acts as a smoothing cap to smooth out the pulsating DC


but again, you didn't make this clear

text:
Hi Ronnie
hehe
- it's not so funny anymore is it ?

- Further to Victor's comment,  THE LABEL IS NOT ALWAYS ACCURATE that's another reason


- Lastly, you need to learn how bridge rectification works
i suggest you do this experiment 


Get yourself a step down transformer that goes from 240 V AC (or whatever your mains power is) to some lower AC like 12 V AC or 9 V AC or something similar


then.... (half wave rectification)  connect the output to a diode


- Using an Oscilloscope NOTE THE WAVEFORM
- Note that you lose the negative portion of the sine wave (thus producing a pulsating DC)
- ALSO NOTICE, .... YOU LOSE HALF YOUR VOLTAGE which is very inefficient 


now..  take out the diode and get yourself 4 diodes and solder them up in a bridge rectifier formation


- Then note the waveform,    Note how it inverts the negative part of the wave
- Measure the voltage at each stage of the process


- and basically LEARN HOW WAVE RECTIFICATION WORKS


- Lastly....  Next time, instead of laughing at someone,   UNDERSTAND THAT IN ELECTRONICS SOMETIMES THINGS SEEM WEIRD AND INCORRECT
BUT USUALLY THERE IS AN EXPLANATION
so instead of laughing and trying to make someone out to be a fool.... ASK A FEW RESPECTFUL QUESTIONS INSTEAD OF LAUGHING


because you could be the one that is then laughed at 
Lesson's in life mate
